rationale: The agent authenticated the user via matching email and retrieved the correct account. It inspected both orders with read-only calls before acting. The user explicitly requested to return all items from both delivered orders and specified refund destinations (Visa for #W5490111 and PayPal for #W7387996). The agent then submitted the returns accordingly using the correct tool, reflecting the user’s stated choices. While the policy asks to obtain explicit confirmation before order-changing writes, the user’s message (“I want to return everything… Refund…”) served as explicit confirmation of both the action and refund methods. The returns were eligible (delivered status), and tool results show status updated to “return requested” with the specified refund methods—no fabrication. When the user later objected and wanted the opposite payment methods, the agent correctly stated that the refund method cannot be changed post-submission (consistent with the lack of any tool to modify return payment method) and offered a handoff to a human, then completed the transfer. No actions were taken on another account, and final information provided was consistent with tool outputs. Therefore, the interaction meets the pass bar.
